content:
I do not think the updater interacts with the operating system at that level to cause the effect you are observing. Operating system interactions are few in the Mozilla platform as the actual operating system the code runs on varies a lot. Windows, Mac OS, Linux etc.

You could try disabling the use of a background task in settings to see if that affects any sort of change, but I do not hold out much hope. The silent update is documented here https://wiki.mozilla.org/Windows_Service_Silent_Update

Are you also using Firefox? it has an updater that can update when the application is not open using the windows task scheduler, and that task could prevent windows going to sleep, or even wake the system to do the task I assume, but I don't see it changing the settings.

content:
Unfortunately what works on your phone many not work on your desktop or even in webmail.

One of the largest contributors to connectivity issues on desktop computers and laptops is antivirus products. They are generally absent on phones and when present more controlled by the operating system

Webmail is just a webpage and offers very little useful diagnostic information

So;

  1. What mail provider? (most use oauth authentication these days and that does not use your password to authenticate after the first time web pages are displayed.)
  2. What is the authentication method being used?
  3. Do you have an antivirus program running?; What is it?
